quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Alcohol at any level is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows your nerves and body functions. This makes you less cautious and makes it harder to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on roads?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as fines for regular traffic violations.
You must slow down in the cone zone.
Only slow down if you think workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should check:

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to police:

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a traffic ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: You must have proof of insurance with you when you drive. Always show your insurance proof and license to a police officer after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian on the road and a vehicle is coming toward you, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one road danger at a time when possible. Slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: You are in a minor crash at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a crash with no injuries, move your vehicle out of traffic if you can do it safely.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots disappear if you have one mirror on each side of your vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots using your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: When parking on a hill:

options.text: One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park.
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: When parking on a hill, always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the road center. If there is a curb, turn your wheels toward it when going downhill, or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed limit in good conditions is 55 mph.
You cannot drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit in good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show traffic laws you must follow. This sign shows the highest speed you can drive on this road. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than this limit.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, you can move back to the right lane when:

options.text: About three seconds have passed.
You can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
You can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on the left, move back to the right lane when you can see the front of that vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes about speed and distance and increases your crash risk. It makes decisions take longer. When fatigued, you could fall asleep while driving and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane mostly because the motorcycle is small and does not use all of the lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Have your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, use a full lane. Do not share the lane with the motorcycle. Moving back too soon can force the rider to swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must give you the right-of-way.
You must give them the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are:

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show specific traffic laws you must follow. They cover direction, lane use, turns, speed, parking, and special situations. They are usually white rectangles with black, red, or green symbols or letters.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Immediately enter the right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, speed up only after you spot a gap in traffic. Generally, stay stopped while waiting for a gap to appear.

questions.question: An orange road sign means:

options.text: There is roadwork ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs show construction areas. Drive carefully and cautiously.

questions.question: Before entering a curve:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the posted speed limit based on road conditions. Reduce speed for curves or hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Turning right at this intersection is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually without applying the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without applying the brakes.
questions.explanation: When tires lose contact with the road and ride on a layer of water, it is called hydroplaning. This can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph in heavy rain. If your vehicle hydroplanes, slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: What is the law about posters and signs on car windows?

options.text: They are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
They are not allowed if they block your view of the road.
They are allowed if they do not contain offensive language.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not allowed if they block your view of the road.
questions.explanation: State law prohibits anything on windows that blocks your view of the road. No signs, posters, or materials may be placed on vehicle windows if they obstruct the driver's clear view.

questions.question: When bad weather or dim light requires your lights on while driving, which should you use?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a dashed white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines mean drivers can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look and listen. Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen. Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, look and listen. Slow down and be ready to stop. Let any trains pass before you go.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Start a left turn from the far left lane of a one-way street.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease your following distance.
Pass through carefully and do not slow down to look at things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass through carefully and do not slow down to look at things.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at things in construction zones. This slowing, called rubbernecking, causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what is allowed?

options.text: Passing from the left.
Passing from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means turns in the direction of the arrow are not allowed. In this case, right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in that direction.
Drivers may turn in that direction after a complete stop.
Drivers may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must remain stopped and wait for a green signal before proceeding in that direction.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: When should you give your name, address, and vehicle registration to other drivers in a collision?

options.text: Only if someone is injured.
Only when damage is over $500.
Every time you are in a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you are in a collision.
questions.explanation: You must stop at every collision. Always give your license and your name, address, and vehicle registration information to other drivers involved, no matter what.

questions.question: What should drivers do if they are worried, nervous, or angry?

options.text: Let someone else drive.
They will be more alert and precise drivers.
They will drive the same as normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If worried, nervous, angry, or upset, let someone else drive. Driving with a distracted mind is never safe.

questions.question: You see a green traffic light but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can get completely across.
Enter and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can get completely across.
questions.explanation: Even if your light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can get all the way through before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: When must vehicles be covered by liability insurance?

options.text: Only on interstate highways.
Only when driven by a minor.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Alabama law requires all motor vehicles on public roads to have liability insurance at all times. This protects drivers involved in accidents.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Cars trying to pass them.
Cars coming straight toward them.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming straight toward them.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must let oncoming vehicles pass first. Turn only when it is safe and you will not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Turn after slowing down and checking for traffic.
Do not turn until the light turns green.
Turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Never turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: What should drivers do at a green traffic signal?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to quickly clear the intersection.
Go straight, turn left, or turn right where allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight, turn left, or turn right where allowed.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you may go straight or turn where allowed. If turning on green, yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?

options.text: When driving a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
When staying within that speed range.
When driving a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When staying within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (within speed limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot hit each other. Crashes often happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: What should drivers do at a red traffic signal?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to quickly clear the intersection.
Continue through without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: Stop at a red light. Remain stopped until the signal turns green.
